bull.b: Record Q3 growth across branded products, coupled with positive adjusted EBITDA, indicates commercial scale is converting into operating earnings. A larger branded mix and sequential momentum can strengthen internal funding capacity and support continued investment in launches, sales coverage, and portfolio expansion over the next several quarters.

VEVYE's prescription, prescriber, and share gains show broadening adoption rather than relying solely on price or inventory timing. The top-three PBM win expands access to previously blocked commercial lives, which can support recurring prescription growth and improve the durability of the dry-eye franchise.

TYRVAYA adds an FDA-approved, drop-free dry-eye therapy to Harrow's existing ocular-surface portfolio and brings experienced commercial personnel. The acquisition broadens product coverage and sales reach, while the company expects more than $30 million of 2027 sales, creating a meaningful medium-term growth platform.

bear.b: Debt rose to about $293 million while equity fell to roughly $29 million, producing approximately 10x debt-to-equity. This sharply limits balance-sheet flexibility, increases reliance on successful product execution and refinancing capacity, and leaves less room to absorb operating setbacks or fund expansion without additional financial pressure.

The latest TTM period reversed from 2025's positive cash generation to approximately $19 million of negative operating cash flow and $20 million of negative free cash flow. Combined with deeper net losses, this raises funding pressure and makes sustained investment more dependent on an earnings recovery.

IHEEZO's loss of pass-through reimbursement in ASC and surgical settings removes an important route to adoption, while management described the ASC market as effectively shut. The restriction can suppress uptake and revenue in that channel, requiring continued execution in-office markets to offset the structural access headwind.
